assemble_report.py.contents:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Assemble scoped final evidence; do not convert unavailable gates to passes."""
import difflib
import hashlib
import json
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
OUT = ROOT / "irc-security-followup-validation"
WORK = ROOT / "irc-security-followup-work"
BASE = ROOT / "irc-security-followup-baseline"
PAIRS = (("onekeyirc-0.1.25", "onekeyirc-0.1.26"),
         ("vipirc-0.7.26", "vipirc-0.7.27"))


def sha(path):
    return hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()


def read_json(path):
    return json.loads(path.read_text())


required = ["final-configure", "final-strict-build", "final-one-sanitize-build",
            "final-vip-idle-harness-normal-build", "final-vip-idle-harness-sanitize-build",
            "final-security-normal", "final-efficiency-normal", "final-session-controls-normal",
            "final-detach-normal", "final-extra-units-build", "final-terminal-live-supported",
            "final-native-session-probe", "final-security-sanitize", "final-session-controls-sanitize",
            "final-notice-normal", "final-terminal-policy-normal", "final-presence-real-sanitize",
            "final-hostile-idle-90s"]
required += ["final-" + x for x in ("test_summary", "test_dcc", "test_editor", "test_nicks",
             "test_credentials", "test_app", "cli", "commands-manual", "terminal-offline",
             "context", "setup", "setup-async", "setup-paths", "autojoin-reconnect", "idle-dcc",
             "rename", "wrapping")]
required += ["final-one-sanitize-" + x for x in ("wrapping", "availability", "notice", "terminal-policy")]
for label in ("normal", "sanitize"):
    required += ["final-vip-idle-" + label + "-" + x for x in
                 ("cli", "commands-manual", "wrapping", "availability", "catchup", "notice", "terminal-policy")]
    required += ["final-full-ui-history-" + label, "final-full-ui-terminal-" + label]
    required += ["final-vip-core-" + label + "-" + x for x in
                 ("build", "test_security_history", "test_session_cli")]

history = read_json(OUT / "followup-gates.json")
latest = {record["name"]: record for record in history}
assert len(required) == len(set(required))
assert not (set(required) - latest.keys()), sorted(set(required) - latest.keys())
for name in required:
    expected = "UNAVAILABLE" if name == "final-native-session-probe" else "PASS"
    assert latest[name]["status"] == expected, (name, latest[name])
gates = [latest[name] for name in required]

static_all = read_json(OUT / "static/results.json")
static = list({item["source"]: item for item in static_all}.values())
for item in static:
    assert item["exit_code"] == 0
    assert sha(ROOT / item["source"]) == item["sha256"], item["source"]
    assert read_json(OUT / "static" / item["log"]) == []

binary_hashes = read_json(OUT / "final-binary-hashes.json")
for rel, expected in binary_hashes.items():
    assert sha(ROOT / rel) == expected, rel

common = sorted({p.name for p in (WORK / PAIRS[0][1] / "src").iterdir() if p.is_file()} &
                {p.name for p in (WORK / PAIRS[1][1] / "src").iterdir() if p.is_file()})
for name in common:
    assert (WORK / PAIRS[0][1] / "src" / name).read_bytes() == (WORK / PAIRS[1][1] / "src" / name).read_bytes(), name

packaging = read_json(OUT / "packaging-validation.json")
assert packaging["status"] == "PASS" and packaging["identical_tested_binary"]
soak = json.loads((OUT / "final-hostile-idle-90s.log").read_text().splitlines()[0])
assert soak["result"] == "PASS"
source_hashes, changes = {}, {}
for old, new in PAIRS:
    source_hashes[new] = {str(p.relative_to(WORK / new)): sha(p)
                          for directory in ("src", "tests")
                          for p in sorted((WORK / new / directory).iterdir())
                          if p.is_file() and p.suffix in (".c", ".h", ".py")}
    changes[new] = {}
    for path in sorted((WORK / new / "src").iterdir()):
        if not path.is_file() or path.suffix not in (".c", ".h"):
            continue
        before = BASE / old / "src" / path.name
        old_bytes = before.read_bytes() if before.exists() else b""
        if old_bytes != path.read_bytes():
            changes[new]["src/" + path.name] = "".join(difflib.unified_diff(
                old_bytes.decode().splitlines(keepends=True), path.read_text().splitlines(keepends=True),
                fromfile=old + "/src/" + path.name, tofile=new + "/src/" + path.name))

evidence = {}
for path in sorted(OUT.rglob("*")):
    if not path.is_file() or path.suffix not in (".json", ".log", ".txt", ".c", ".py"):
        continue
    rel = path.relative_to(OUT)
    if len(rel.parts) > 1 and rel.parts[0] not in ("network", "local", "dcc", "static", "static-initial"):
        continue
    if path.name in ("report-body.txt", "followup-report-sections.txt", "release-integrity.json") or path.stat().st_size > 2_000_000:
        continue
    evidence[str(rel)] = dict(sha256=sha(path), size_bytes=path.stat().st_size,
                             contents=path.read_text(errors="replace"))

result = dict(
    schema_version=1, date_utc="2026-11-16", releases=[new for old, new in PAIRS],
    status="PASS_FOR_EXECUTED_SCOPE_WITH_EXPLICIT_UNAVAILABLE_PLATFORM_GATES",
    scope="Source follow-up; local/private fixtures only; no public IRC traffic or live deployment",
    summary=dict(passed_gate_groups=sum(g["status"] == "PASS" for g in gates),
                 unavailable_gate_groups=sum(g["status"] == "UNAVAILABLE" for g in gates),
                 failed_final_gate_groups=0, static_translation_units=len(static),
                 static_diagnostics=0, identical_common_source_files=len(common)),
    final_gates=gates, all_gate_attempts=history,
    source_hashes=source_hashes, shared_source_parity=common,
    tested_binary_hashes=binary_hashes, static_analysis=static,
    environment=read_json(OUT / "environment.json"),
    hostile_idle_soak=soak,
    packaging_validation=packaging,
    limitations=[
        "Linux execution, no native OpenBSD runtime.",
        "Named AF_UNIX creation returns EPERM; native SCM_RIGHTS/session registry lifecycle unavailable.",
        "Full wide-curses configure fails; vipirc -i harness and extracted full-UI boundaries are separately scoped.",
        "Real GnuPG keyring/agent integration not established; controlled helper fixtures only.",
        "LeakSanitizer unavailable under tracing; ASan/UBSan runs use detect_leaks=0.",
        "Short hostile soak and sampled CPU comparisons do not establish indefinite reliability.",
        "Trusted same UID/root/kernel/terminal/TLS library; classic DCC and optional logs remain plaintext.",
    ],
    development_evidence_note=(
        "Embedded records include expected baseline failures, superseded development snapshots and fixture adjustments. "
        "In particular the early local security review preceded the later config.c terminal-policy change. "
        "Final_gates and source_hashes define the released candidate; historical hashes remain historical."),
    source_changes=changes, evidence_documents=evidence,
)

count = result["summary"]
header = f"""SECURITY FOLLOW-UP AND TERMINAL POLICY REVIEW
Date: 2026-11-16 UTC
Releases: onekeyirc 0.1.26 and vipirc 0.7.27
Compared with: onekeyirc 0.1.25 and vipirc 0.7.26

RESULT AND SCOPE

The executed release gates passed. Confirmed findings were fixed in the
shared core and both affected frontends. The full requested local notice
and default-off terminal signal override are included. This is a bounded
source review with reproducible regressions, not a security certification.

Final gate groups: {count['passed_gate_groups']} PASS, {count['unavailable_gate_groups']} UNAVAILABLE, 0 FAIL.
The unavailable group is native AF_UNIX session lifecycle; additional
full-curses, native OpenBSD, real GnuPG and leak-scanning limits are explained
below. A passing group may contain several C binaries or terminal cases.
No full unrestricted make check or native OpenBSD pass is claimed.

The threat model includes hostile IRC/server text, terminal-control bytes,
malformed DCC traffic and offers, resource pressure, and other local UIDs.
The account itself, administrator/kernel, executable, terminal, TLS library
and trust store remain trusted. Local tests used an offline simulator,
private temporary files, real PTYs and loopback TCP; they did not contact
the public IRC network or modify a user's running worker.

wrapped chat, history recall and managed hangup handling remain included.

and binary hashes, source diffs, and scoped development snapshots. Evidence

to irc-security-followup-validation/. New regression sources are in tests/.

boundaries, managed hangup/detach fixtures, application/credential/editor/DCC
units, CLI and embedded manual consistency, offline/live terminal behavior,
setup and asynchronous helpers, reconnect/autojoin, rename, wrapping, pinned
destinations, catch-up, slow terminal handling and retained history.

Sanitizer gates cover the security and session-control suites, notice delivery,
credential child lifecycle, DCC injected failures, real automatic-away retry
availability, wrapping, reviewed-message availability and terminal signal
policy. vipirc -i uses real main/core/minimalist code with aborting unused
curses entry points. Full UI history and terminal policy have separate exact
production-boundary tests; presentation/curses substitutions are disclosed.

and executed normally and with ASan/UBSan.

The 90-second hostile-idle gate exercises hostile display payloads and malformed
UTF-8 inside correctly framed IRC traffic, bounded state, resource behavior, continued PING handling and process cleanup.

sampling was unavailable in this soak; direct cleanup assertions exist in
the focused descriptor/child/DCC fixtures instead.

uptime or resistance to all resource-exhaustion attacks.

diagnostics. All {len(common)} common src files match byte-for-byte across the
two source releases. This is bounded coverage, not a proof of memory safety.

byte-for-byte. A private DESTDIR installation verified version, embedded manual,
file modes and installed contents; uninstall left no files. Packaging uses the

excluding built binaries and unrelated workspace data. Each archive contains

member's bytes, type and mode. The outside .sha256 file covers both source
archives and this standalone report. Checksums detect changed bytes; they are

The real-shell signal gate needs Python 3 and bash; those are test dependencies,

uses the system TLS implementation; these source changes do not update a VPS's

FOLLOW-UP DCC AND LOG BOUNDARY REVIEW

No new confirmed production DCC defect. DCC sources remain byte-identical to
baseline .25. New tests/test_dcc_adversarial.c passes the untouched baseline,
current candidate, and ASan/UBSan (detect_leaks=0).

The test uses actual private files and loopback TCP lifecycle. Short file and
socket writes, EINTR/EAGAIN, ENOSPC and EMFILE are explicitly injected at syscall
boundaries to exercise hard-to-arrange failure states. Real EOF/reset, fragmented
and invalid ACKs, byte-exact transfer data, private file modes, partial-file
cleanup, cancellation, descriptor closure and concurrent-transfer isolation are
checked. Deadline advancement is simulated through the existing public clock
argument. No public network traffic was sent.

The first sanitizer run with leak scanning enabled exited 134 because this
traced environment cannot run LeakSanitizer. Its exact failure is retained.
ASan/UBSan subsequently passed with leak scanning disabled. Descriptor/file
cleanup assertions remain active; this is not a heap-leak certification.

Read-only log/catch-up review found a reproducible local integrity problem:
last_own_log_offset alone could match a replacement private log with the same
channel prefix, making /catchup claim the old sent-message anchor while the new
inode did not contain it. The standalone baseline proof calls production
begin_catchup using a seeded valid runtime anchor and actual local filesystem
rotation. It does not demonstrate an attacker-only IRC trigger. Root delegated
its fix and final regression coverage to the local security reviewer.

Known design limits remain: unencrypted/unauthenticated classic DCC, explicit
acceptance of offered endpoints including private addresses, synchronous regular
file I/O, in-place source mutation by local writers, per-file limits rather than
space quotas, and no isolation from same-UID/root filesystem control.

Machine-readable commands, results, test distinctions and hashes are in
 dcc-results.json. No metadata, Makefile or DCC production files were changed
by this reviewer.

dcc/notice-presence-review.txt.contents:
READ-ONLY INDEPENDENT NOTICE AND PRESENCE REVIEW

Reviewed Client.session_notice_shown, the new idle stream_output block, the
vipirc ui main-loop insertion, idle output/terminal lifecycle and history import,
and the automatic-away retry implementation plus test_security_presence.c.
No broad builds or tests were run for this second review.

Concrete notice edge cases reported to root for disposition:
1. The idle flag was committed when the reminder entered the output queue,
   before output_flush confirmed delivery. If the first write blocks or fails
   and terminal loss discards that queue, the resumed worker could have shown=1
   although the reminder was never written. An initially detached worker
   otherwise leaves the flag unset until WATCH with an attached terminal.
2. The full-screen insertion used app_log. That saves the reminder in canonical
   App history and, when logging was already enabled, appends it to the private
   persistent log. Switching full-screen to idle imports this history through
   attach_apps; a context replay can show the historical reminder even though
   the Client flag prevents another insertion. Idle's direct output does not
   have that retention behavior. No reminder path sends IRC output.

The existing Client object survives server changes, reconnects and frontend
switches, so the chosen flag ownership is appropriate. Main-screen/detached
checks defer full-screen insertion while dialogs or no terminal are active.

Automatic-away retry review found no new defect. Failed output schedules a
bounded retry and both scheduling and presence advancement honor it. Success,
local activity and disconnect/reconnect reset the deadline. Manual-away wins;
PING, normal queued output and autocommands are processed outside this retry
wait. Valid loaded config requires nonempty enabled away messages, and normal
registered transport lifecycle avoids the unchanged early-return cases that
otherwise lack retry scheduling. The deterministic presence regression checks
limit reduction, queue pressure, manual-away precedence, deadline progress,
PING and successful recovery.

These observations describe the reviewed intermediate source, not a claim
about later root corrections or final full-curses runtime validation.

ROOT DISPOSITION
Full UI normal-history insertion is deliberate: one insertion per worker, with
ordinary history redisplay and existing opt-in persistence. That is not treated
as a duplicate announcement. Root will correct idle delivery acknowledgement
and put operational/error notices ahead of the reminder. No additional notice
network-send or draft mutation path was identified.

FINAL READ-ONLY RECHECK
Root's completed idle change tracks the queued byte count through the end of
the reminder, including older bytes ahead of it. Successful writes decrement
that count and commit the Client flag only after the last reminder byte. All
three production queue-discard sites reset pending delivery; ordinary queue
compaction and appended data do not disturb the count. The focused real-pipe
test covers a partial write, explicit EAGAIN, queue discard/retry, COMPOSE
deferral, operational notice ordering and last-byte completion. No additional
security or lifecycle issue found in this final diff. No extra tests run by
this reviewer.

The local reviewer's final anchor fix and its regression additions were also
independently reviewed. Bounds, file identity, bounded full-record read, append
and close success gating, and the existing memory fallback are coherent. The
checksum is explicitly accidental-change detection, not authentication.

REAL-WORKER AUTOMATIC-AWAY AVAILABILITY CHECK

New portable gate: tests/test_presence_availability.py
Run: python3 tests/test_presence_availability.py --fixture build/idle_hangup_fixture

The gate uses the existing LossSession/private loopback fixture. Through the
actual command UI it enables background away and sets its message to 100 A
bytes. The local server advertises LINELEN=64; a PING barrier establishes that
this limit was processed. Managed SIGHUP then detaches the real worker and
makes its configured automatic-away line unsendable. The measurement runs for
three seconds with periodic PINGs. Descriptor reattachment exposes retained
failure statuses after the timed interval. Native AF_UNIX session handshakes
are not exercised; initial managed-state setup and reattachment are fixtures.

Both comparative fixtures were compiled with strict warnings and -O2 from
unchanged input snapshots. Before/after hashes and exact compiler arguments
are in presence-build-results.json. Baseline is untouched .25; candidate is
.26 after the network reviewer confirmed the shared app/idle changes settled.

Observed normal comparison:
- Baseline: 3.000 sampled worker CPU seconds in 3.000159 wall seconds; whole
  child lifetime 3.101306 CPU seconds. Forty retained failure notices. Gate
  exited 1 for busy-loop CPU consumption and unbounded retry status.
- Candidate: 0.000 sampled worker CPU seconds in 3.000112 wall seconds; whole
  child lifetime 0.011893 CPU seconds. Four retained failure notices. Gate
  exited 0.
- Both answered all nine measured PINGs. Maximum observed latency was
  0.516 ms for baseline and 0.308 ms for candidate. Neither sent AWAY, chat
  or an outgoing frame exceeding the reduced 64-byte wire limit.

The /proc CPU clock resolution was 0.01 seconds (100 ticks/second). Zero
sampled CPU means no observable tick increment; it does not mean literally
zero execution. process_stats verified parent/namespace PID and process start
identity. Executable-link comparison was unavailable (exe_verified=false).
The normal comparison completed before the network reviewer's later compiler
burst. The retained-notice count is bounded replayed history, not the total
number of status callbacks; baseline history had already rolled over.

The portable fallback was also exercised by forcing only the test helper's
verified /proc sampler to report unavailable. The real candidate worker and
resource.getrusage child accounting remained active. That run passed with
0.012624 whole-child CPU seconds, four retained failure notices, nine PINGs
and maximum latency 5.339 ms. It is not used for the normal CPU comparison.

No production files were changed by this task. Candidate normal integration
should rerun the gate against the final source-frozen hangup fixture.

TERMINAL SIGNAL POLICY: REAL SHELL / PTY REGRESSION

New tests/test_terminal_signals.py is identical in both candidate source trees.
Interface: --binary PATH, optional --full for vipirc --idle, optional --case.
No production files were edited by this reviewer and no primary binary was
rebuilt by this task. Root supplied the newly built normal binaries.

The three-case normal gate passed for onekeyirc .26 and vipirc -i .27:
1. The option is omitted and the invoking shell has -isig. Runtime keeps ISIG
   off. Literal Ctrl-C, Ctrl-Z and Ctrl-backslash are inert at welcome and in a
   composed draft; the draft/caret remain unchanged. Explicit SIGTERM exits 143.
2. The option is explicitly false and the invoking shell enables isig with
   VINTR=Ctrl-G, VSUSP=Ctrl-], VQUIT=Ctrl-X. Default signal bytes remain inert.
   Remapped suspend produces real SIGTSTP/fg at welcome and in the composer,
   retaining the draft and moved caret; remapped interrupt exits 130.
3. The option is true while the invoking shell has -isig and the same custom
   mappings. Runtime enables ISIG without changing mapping bytes. The same
   real suspension/resume checks pass; remapped quit exits 131. Restoration
   returns ISIG to the inherited disabled state.

Each frontend checks seven complete termios plus input/output descriptor-flag
restorations before bash can restore its own terminal settings: one exit in
case 1, and two real stops plus one exit in each mapped case. The foreground
job is deliberately non-orphaned. A private Python launcher waits for the real
client's stopped/exit state, records its tty, then stops itself for ordinary
shell fg. It does not replace application tty calls or signal handlers. The
shell's original settings are separately restored at the end of each case.

The initial harness set mappings only inside the job; bash correctly restored
its older shell mappings on fg. That fixture issue was corrected by applying
stty in the actual parent shell before launch. No signal, caret or exact-tty
assertion was weakened. The intermediate failure is retained separately as
terminal-signals-shell-fixture-adjustment.log/results.json and is not a
production defect.

With the finalized harness, untouched .25 fails the default -isig case because
its terminal startup enables ISIG unconditionally. That proof uses the
previously built private .25 hangup fixture with managed substitution disabled;
there was no additional baseline compilation or public network access.

Normal run commands, binary/test hashes and per-case results are in
terminal-signals-results.json. The finalized baseline proof is in
terminal-signals-baseline-final-results.json and its matching log. Root will
run final sanitizer versions. No full-curses runtime or native AF_UNIX session
handshake coverage is claimed by this test.

network/final-findings.txt.contents:
Network, application, authentication and command-history follow-up
Date: 2026-11-16 UTC
Released baselines: onekeyirc 0.1.25 and vipirc 0.7.26
Working releases: onekeyirc 0.1.26 and vipirc 0.7.27

Scope and result

Reviewed src/net.c, src/protocol.c, src/app.c and src/autocommands.c, then
followed recognized private credential commands through the minimalist and
full frontend histories. Confirmed two defect families: an expired automatic
away retry deadline that can keep the event loop busy, and inconsistent
command-history privacy classification. No new TLS identity-verification,
authentication-handshake bypass, IRC command injection or cross-host
credential-copy defect was confirmed in this review. That negative result is
a source-review result, not a proof that those boundaries have no defects.

1. Failed automatic away could drive continuous polling

A connected server can advertise LINELEN=64. A valid configured 100-byte
automatic-away message then cannot fit. At local-idle expiry, or immediately
when background-away starts, queuing AWAY fails and automatic_away remains
NONE. The old timer remains due, so app_timeout keeps returning zero and the
application repeats the failed attempt without any further network input.
The trigger needs the selected server's line-limit advertisement and an
enabled local away setting whose message does not fit; ordinary channel text
does not set LINELEN. Temporary control-queue exhaustion is another reason
the same automatic attempt can fail.

The deterministic released-baseline probe ran 1,000 state-machine iterations
without advancing time. Local-idle mode produced 1,000 zero timeouts and
1,000 status callbacks; background mode produced 1,000 zero timeouts and
1,001 callbacks, including its initial attempt. Neither queued or sent AWAY.
With the fix, local-idle has its one expected initially expired timeout and
one failure callback; background has zero repeated zero timeouts and one
failure callback. See presence-baseline.log and presence-fixed.log.

The fix stores a one-second retry deadline, includes it in poll scheduling,
and resets it after successful automatic away, local activity or reconnect.
The focused test verifies exact 999/1,000 ms boundaries, normal PING/PONG
during the wait, recovery after LINELEN or queue capacity changes, no repeated
successful AWAY, idle activity/reconnect reset and manual-away priority.
The test uses deterministic transport and time; its loop counts are not a
wall-clock CPU benchmark. The DCC reviewer separately supplied a real worker
CPU/PING comparison; use that reviewer's recorded results for timing claims.

2. Private credential commands could enter command recall

The core recognizes repeated and standalone leading colons before private
authentication verbs. The old idle history filter stripped only one colon.
Three accepted examples were therefore recordable by the idle frontend:
::IDENTIFY, : : IDENTIFY, and : LOGIN after /msg or /privmsg to CustomAuthBot.
The released full frontend's syntax filter already rejected these forms.
The idle lexical normalization now matches the core's leading space/colon
handling. Case variants, command aliases, numeric account arguments and
ordinary-text positive controls are covered.

A second mismatch affected both histories. One logical command can begin
with ordinary HELP text, fill exactly one IRC payload, then begin the next
wire payload with IDENTIFY. The core already classifies this actual send
plan as credential-bearing, but both history filters inspected only the
first word of the original command. The baseline probe retained this line;
the extracted production full-UI send/remember path also failed with
"messages=2 private=1 retained_delta=1". See history-baseline.log and
ui-history-baseline.log. This demonstrates in-process command-recall
retention, not credential transmission to an unintended peer or a disk leak.

The new pure app_plan_history_safe function recomputes and validates bounded
logical/wire slices and uses the existing core privacy classifier. Both
frontends pass the exact successful message plan to their history gate.
Non-message commands pass no plan. Canonical command-name usage counts
remain available and do not store arguments. Full-UI success, cancellation,
failure and new-command entry clear obsolete pending-plan state while the
editor draft remains available where needed.

The candidate split probe deliberately still shows syntax-only allowances
of 1: a syntax-only function has no wire budget. The added actual-plan gate
returns 0 and both combined gates return 0. Actual idle direct/review tests
and extracted full-UI direct/review/remember tests verify the complete gate,
with ordinary single/split history, subsequent commands and usage counters
preserved. Invalid count, slice, budget and unterminated-string plans fail
closed in the pure helper. Unknown custom authentication syntax and
arbitrary secrets in ordinary prose are outside the existing recognizer's
scope; this is not a promise to erase all secrets from process memory.

Validation and limits

The four new focused gates passed strict normal builds and AddressSanitizer
plus UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer: test_security_presence.c,
test_security_history.c, test_security_history_flow.c, and vipirc's
test_security_ui_history.py. ASan leak detection was disabled. The history
fixtures use the production offline simulator and accepted queues, with no
public network or real credentials. The full-UI test compiles unchanged
selected production blocks with the actual App, commands, editor and prompt
history code; presentation callbacks are inert. It verifies the state and
privacy boundary and does not claim curses rendering, terminal dispatch or
native OpenBSD execution. Root owns final aggregate/release validation.

Transport/authentication review also checked strict TLS host/IP verification
and failure handling, bounded framing and sanitization, CAP/SASL ordering,
credential queue suppression, complete-batch send revalidation, connection
generation checks, current line limits, and preservation of an already
in-flight TLS retry buffer. No transport policy was weakened. The local
reviewer separately checked endpoint credential inheritance and the on-disk
credential/IPC boundary. Existing workers must be restarted to execute these
fixes after installing the new binaries.

Changed files for this contribution

Shared production: src/app.c, src/app.h, src/idle.c, src/idle_commands.c.
Full-UI production: src/ui.c, src/prompt.c, src/prompt.h.
Shared tests: tests/test_security_presence.c, tests/test_security_history.c,
tests/test_security_history_flow.c.
Full-UI test: tests/test_security_ui_history.py.
No net.c, protocol.c or autocommands.c production changes were needed.
The shared files also contain disjoint root/local notice and log-anchor
changes; those are documented by their owners. Latest shared source/test
contents were mirrored and byte-for-byte parity checked between candidates.

package_release.py.contents:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Create source-only packages from the verified upstream file inventories."""
from datetime import datetime, timezone
import gzip
import hashlib
import io
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import shutil
import stat
import subprocess
import sys
import tarfile
import time

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
OUT = ROOT / "irc-security-followup-validation"
WORK = ROOT / "irc-security-followup-work"
BASE = ROOT / "irc-security-followup-baseline"
STAGE = ROOT / "irc-security-followup-release-staging"
RELEASE = ROOT / "irc-security-followup-release"
PAIRS = (("onekeyirc-0.1.25", "onekeyirc-0.1.26"),
         ("vipirc-0.7.26", "vipirc-0.7.27"))
EXTRA = ("tests/test_security_presence.c", "tests/test_security_history.c",
         "tests/test_security_history_flow.c", "tests/test_dcc_adversarial.c",
         "tests/test_credential_lifecycle.c", "tests/test_notice_delivery.c",
         "tests/test_session_notice.py", "tests/test_presence_availability.py",
         "tests/test_terminal_signals.py", "doc/SECURITY-FOLLOWUP-2026-11-16.txt",
         "doc/FOLLOWUP-TEST-RESULTS.json")
VIP_EXTRA = ("tests/test_security_ui_history.py", "tests/test_ui_terminal_signals.py")

EPOCH = int(datetime(2026, 11, 16, tzinfo=timezone.utc).timestamp())


def digest(path):
    return hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()


def paths(old):
    entries = json.loads((BASE/old/"SOURCE-MANIFEST.json").read_text())["files"]
    extra = EXTRA + (VIP_EXTRA if old.startswith("vipirc") else ())
    result = sorted(set(e["path"] for e in entries) | set(extra))
    assert len(result) == len(entries) + len(extra)
    return result


def source_hashes(tree):
    return {p.name: digest(p) for p in sorted((tree/"src").iterdir())
            if p.suffix in (".c", ".h")}


def stage():
    STAGE.mkdir(exist_ok=False)
    for old, new in PAIRS:
        for rel in paths(old):
            src, dst = WORK/new/rel, STAGE/new/rel
            assert src.is_file() and not src.is_symlink(), src
            dst.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            shutil.copy2(src, dst)
        print("STAGED " + new + " " + str(len(paths(old))) + " source files", flush=True)


def validate():
    tree = STAGE/"onekeyirc-0.1.26"
    install = OUT/"private-install-root"
    install.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    assert not any(p.is_file() or p.is_symlink() for p in install.rglob("*"))
    env = dict(os.environ, CPPFLAGS="-D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=2",
               CFLAGS="-O2 -Werror -fstack-protector-strong -Wformat=2 -Werror=format-security -fPIE",
               LDFLAGS="-pie -Wl,-z,relro -Wl,-z,now -Wl,-z,noexecstack")
    records = []
    for name, cmd in (
        ("configure", ["./configure"]),
        ("strict-build", ["make", "onekeyirc"]),
        ("install", ["make", "install", "DESTDIR="+str(install)])):
        start = time.monotonic()
        log = OUT/("package-"+name+".log")
        with log.open("wb") as stream:
            p = subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=tree, env=env, stdout=stream,
                               stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, timeout=180)
        records.append(dict(name=name, command=cmd, exit_code=p.returncode,
                            seconds=round(time.monotonic()-start,3), log=log.name))
        assert p.returncode == 0, log.read_text()
    installed = []
    for p in sorted(install.rglob("*")):
        if p.is_file():
            rel = p.relative_to(install)
            expected = 0o755 if str(rel).endswith("/bin/onekeyirc") else 0o644
            assert stat.S_IMODE(p.stat().st_mode) == expected, p
            installed.append(dict(path=str(rel), mode=oct(expected), sha256=digest(p)))
    for name in ("SECURITY-FOLLOWUP-2026-11-16.txt", "FOLLOWUP-TEST-RESULTS.json"):
        assert (install/"usr/local/share/doc/onekeyirc"/name).read_bytes() == (tree/"doc"/name).read_bytes()
    assert (install/"usr/local/bin/onekeyirc").read_bytes() == (tree/"onekeyirc").read_bytes()
    version_output = subprocess.check_output([str(tree/"onekeyirc"), "--version"], env=env).decode()
    version = version_output.splitlines()[0]
    assert version == "onekeyirc 0.1.26", version
    manual = subprocess.check_output([str(tree/"onekeyirc"), "--manual"], env=env)
    assert manual == (tree/"doc/onekeyirc-manual.txt").read_bytes()
    with (OUT/"package-uninstall.log").open("wb") as stream:
        p = subprocess.run(["make", "uninstall", "DESTDIR="+str(install)],
                           cwd=tree, env=env, stdout=stream, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, timeout=30)
    assert p.returncode == 0
    assert not any(p.is_file() or p.is_symlink() for p in install.rglob("*"))
    result = dict(status="PASS", scope="clean standalone source build and private DESTDIR install/uninstall; no host installation",
                  records=records, installed_files=installed, version=version, version_output=version_output,
                  manual_matches=True, uninstall_left_files=False,
                  tested_binary_sha256=digest(WORK/"onekeyirc-0.1.26/onekeyirc"),
                  staged_binary_sha256=digest(tree/"onekeyirc"),
                  identical_tested_binary=digest(tree/"onekeyirc")==digest(WORK/"onekeyirc-0.1.26/onekeyirc"),
                  source_hashes={new:source_hashes(STAGE/new) for _,new in PAIRS},
                  validated_file_sha256={new:{rel:digest(STAGE/new/rel) for rel in paths(old)
                      if rel not in ("doc/SECURITY-FOLLOWUP-2026-11-16.txt","doc/FOLLOWUP-TEST-RESULTS.json","doc/VALIDATION.txt")}
                      for old,new in PAIRS},
                  note="Initial staged installation precedes insertion of packaging evidence into audit documents. Final finalized-document installation is checked again during archive creation.")
    (OUT/"packaging-validation.json").write_text(json.dumps(result,indent=2)+"\n")
    print("PASS: clean build, version/manual, private installation modes/content, and uninstall", flush=True)
    print("Bit-identical to tested onekeyirc binary: " + str(result["identical_tested_binary"]), flush=True)


def finish():
    validation = json.loads((OUT/"packaging-validation.json").read_text())
    assert validation["status"] == "PASS"
    RELEASE.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    archive_results = []
    for old, new in PAIRS:
        tree = STAGE/new
        assert source_hashes(WORK/new) == validation["source_hashes"][new], "source changed after staged validation"
        for rel, expected in validation["validated_file_sha256"][new].items():
            assert digest(WORK/new/rel) == expected, "validated file changed: "+rel
        for rel in paths(old):
            shutil.copy2(WORK/new/rel, tree/rel)
        if new == "onekeyirc-0.1.26":
            install = OUT/"private-install-root"
            assert not any(p.is_file() or p.is_symlink() for p in install.rglob("*"))
            with (OUT/"package-final-doc-install.log").open("wb") as stream:
                subprocess.run(["make","install","DESTDIR="+str(install)], cwd=tree,
                               stdout=stream,stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,check=True,timeout=30)
            installed = {str(p.relative_to(install)):p for p in install.rglob("*") if p.is_file()}
            assert set(installed) == {r["path"] for r in validation["installed_files"]}
            for rel, actual in installed.items():
                if rel.endswith("/bin/onekeyirc"):
                    source=tree/"onekeyirc"; mode=0o755
                elif "/man/man1/" in rel:
                    source=tree/"doc/onekeyirc.1"; mode=0o644
                else:
                    name=actual.name;mode=0o644
                    candidates=[tree/name,tree/"doc"/name,tree/"examples"/name]
                    source=next(p for p in candidates if p.is_file())
                assert not actual.is_symlink() and stat.S_IMODE(actual.stat().st_mode)==mode
                assert actual.read_bytes()==source.read_bytes(),rel
            with (OUT/"package-final-doc-uninstall.log").open("wb") as stream:
                subprocess.run(["make","uninstall","DESTDIR="+str(install)],cwd=tree,
                               stdout=stream,stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,check=True,timeout=30)
            assert not any(p.is_file() or p.is_symlink() for p in install.rglob("*"))
        entries = [dict(path=rel, sha256=digest(tree/rel), size_bytes=(tree/rel).stat().st_size,
                        mode=format(stat.S_IMODE((tree/rel).stat().st_mode), "04o")) for rel in paths(old)]
        (tree/"SOURCE-MANIFEST.json").write_text(json.dumps(dict(release=new,files=entries),indent=2)+"\n")
        sha_paths = paths(old)+["SOURCE-MANIFEST.json"]
        (tree/"SHA256SUMS").write_text("".join(digest(tree/rel)+"  "+rel+"\n" for rel in sorted(sha_paths)))
        all_paths = paths(old)+["SOURCE-MANIFEST.json","SHA256SUMS"]
        dirs = {Path(new)}
        for rel in all_paths:
            parent = Path(new)/Path(rel).parent
            while str(parent) != ".":
                dirs.add(parent)
                parent=parent.parent
        target = RELEASE/(new+"-source.tar.gz")
        with target.open("wb") as raw:
            with gzip.GzipFile(filename="", mode="wb", fileobj=raw, mtime=EPOCH) as compressed:
                with tarfile.open(fileobj=compressed, mode="w", format=tarfile.USTAR_FORMAT) as tar:
                    for directory in sorted(dirs):
                        item=tarfile.TarInfo(str(directory));item.type=tarfile.DIRTYPE
                        item.mode=0o755;item.mtime=EPOCH;tar.addfile(item)
                    for rel in sorted(all_paths):
                        data=(tree/rel).read_bytes();item=tarfile.TarInfo(new+"/"+rel)
                        item.size=len(data);item.mode=stat.S_IMODE((tree/rel).stat().st_mode)
                        item.mtime=EPOCH;tar.addfile(item,io.BytesIO(data))
        with tarfile.open(target,"r:gz") as tar:
            members={m.name:m for m in tar.getmembers() if m.isfile()}
            assert set(members)=={new+"/"+p for p in all_paths}
            assert all(m.isdir() or m.isfile() for m in tar.getmembers())
            for rel in all_paths:
                m=members[new+"/"+rel]
                assert tar.extractfile(m).read()==(tree/rel).read_bytes()
                assert m.mode==stat.S_IMODE((tree/rel).stat().st_mode)
        archive_results.append(dict(file=target.name,sha256=digest(target),size_bytes=target.stat().st_size,
                                    source_files=len(entries),integrity="PASS"))
    report=RELEASE/"onekeyirc-0.1.26-security-followup.txt"
    shutil.copy2(WORK/"onekeyirc-0.1.26/doc/SECURITY-FOLLOWUP-2026-11-16.txt",report)
    sums=RELEASE/"vipirc-0.7.27-onekeyirc-0.1.26.sha256"
    delivered=[RELEASE/a["file"] for a in archive_results]+[report]
    sums.write_text("".join(digest(p)+"  "+p.name+"\n" for p in delivered))
    (OUT/"release-integrity.json").write_text(json.dumps(dict(archives=archive_results,
        report_sha256=digest(report),checksum_sha256=digest(sums),checksum_file=sums.name,
        finalized_document_installation="PASS"),indent=2)+"\n")
    print(json.dumps(archive_results,indent=2),flush=True)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    for phase in sys.argv[1:]:
        globals()[phase]()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Record exact supported release gates without suppressing assertions."""
import hashlib
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
import sys
import time

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
OUT = ROOT / "irc-security-followup-validation"
ONE = ROOT / "irc-security-followup-work/onekeyirc-0.1.26"
VIP = ROOT / "irc-security-followup-work/vipirc-0.7.27"
ENV = dict(os.environ, ASAN_OPTIONS="detect_leaks=0:halt_on_error=1",
           UBSAN_OPTIONS="halt_on_error=1:print_stacktrace=1",
           ONEKEY_BINARY=str(ONE / "onekeyirc"), VIPIRC_IDLE_BINARY="")
RESULT = OUT / "followup-gates.json"
records = json.loads(RESULT.read_text()) if RESULT.exists() else []


def run(name, command, cwd=ONE, env=None, timeout=300, accepted=(0,)):
    force = os.environ.get("AUDIT_RERUN", "").split(",")
    prior = next((r for r in reversed(records) if r["name"] == name), None)
    if (os.environ.get("AUDIT_SKIP_PASS") == "1" and name not in force and
            prior and prior["status"] == "PASS"):
        print("RETAIN previous PASS " + name, flush=True)
        return
    log = OUT / (name + ".log")
    if log.exists():
        number = sum(r["name"] == name for r in records)
        previous = OUT / (name + ".previous-" + str(number) + ".log")
        previous.write_bytes(log.read_bytes())
        if prior:
            prior["log"] = previous.name
    started = time.monotonic()
    print("RUN " + name, flush=True)
    with log.open("wb") as stream:
        result = subprocess.run(command, cwd=cwd, env=env or ENV, stdout=stream,
                                stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, timeout=timeout)
    record = dict(name=name, command=command, cwd=str(cwd),
                  seconds=round(time.monotonic()-started, 3),
                  exit_code=result.returncode, log=log.name,
                  status="UNAVAILABLE" if result.returncode == 77 else
                         "PASS" if result.returncode == 0 else "FAIL")
    records.append(record)
    RESULT.write_text(json.dumps(records, indent=2) + "\n")
    print(record["status"] + " " + name + " " + str(record["seconds"]) + "s", flush=True)
    if result.returncode not in accepted:
        print(log.read_text(errors="replace")[-9000:], flush=True)
        raise SystemExit(result.returncode or 1)


def build():
    buildenv = dict(ENV, CPPFLAGS="-D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=2",
                    CFLAGS="-O2 -Werror -fstack-protector-strong -Wformat=2 -Werror=format-security -fPIE",
                    LDFLAGS="-pie -Wl,-z,relro -Wl,-z,now -Wl,-z,noexecstack")
    run("final-configure", ["./configure"], env=buildenv)
    run("final-strict-build", ["make", "onekeyirc"], env=buildenv)
    stub = OUT / "unused_curses_entrypoints.c"
    stub.write_text('''#include <stdlib.h>
#include "ui.h"
int ui_welcome(int force) { (void)force; abort(); }
int ui_run_session(Client *c, Background *b, DccManager *d, int start,
                   int connect, int no_connect, int *next) {
    (void)c; (void)b; (void)d; (void)start; (void)connect;
    (void)no_connect; (void)next; abort();
}
''')
    src = next(line.split("=",1)[1].split() for line in
               (ONE/"Makefile.in").read_text().splitlines() if line.startswith("SRC = "))
    base = ["cc", "-D_POSIX_C_SOURCE=200809L", "-D_XOPEN_SOURCE=700",
            "-D_XOPEN_SOURCE_EXTENDED=1", "-std=c11", "-Wall", "-Wextra",
            "-Wpedantic", "-Werror", "-Wformat=2", "-Werror=format-security", "-Isrc"]
    hard = ["-O2", "-D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=2", "-fstack-protector-strong", "-fPIE",
            "-pie", "-Wl,-z,relro", "-Wl,-z,now", "-Wl,-z,noexecstack"]
    san = ["-O1", "-g", "-fsanitize=address,undefined", "-fno-omit-frame-pointer"]
    run("final-one-sanitize-build", base + san + ["-DONEKEY_ONLY", "-o",
        str(OUT/"onekeyirc-sanitize")] + src + ["-lssl", "-lcrypto"])
    for label, flags in (("normal", hard), ("sanitize", san)):
        run("final-vip-idle-harness-"+label+"-build", base+flags+["-o",
            str(OUT/("vipirc-idle-"+label))]+src+["src/manual.c", str(stub),
            "-lssl", "-lcrypto"], cwd=VIP)
    for binary, args, target in (
        (ONE/"onekeyirc", ["--manual"], ONE/"doc/onekeyirc-manual.txt"),
        (OUT/"vipirc-idle-normal", ["-i", "--manual"], VIP/"doc/vipirc-idle-manual.txt")):
        result = subprocess.run([str(binary), *args], capture_output=True, env=ENV, check=True)
        target.write_bytes(result.stdout)
    # The embedded full manual must match its maintained plain-text source.
    full = subprocess.run([str(OUT/"vipirc-idle-normal"), "--manual"],
                          capture_output=True, env=ENV, check=True)
    assert full.stdout == (VIP/"doc/manual.txt").read_bytes(), "full manual embedding mismatch"
    hashes = {str(p.relative_to(ROOT)): hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
              for p in [ONE/"onekeyirc", OUT/"onekeyirc-sanitize",
                        OUT/"vipirc-idle-normal", OUT/"vipirc-idle-sanitize"]}
    (OUT/"final-binary-hashes.json").write_text(json.dumps(hashes, indent=2)+"\n")


def normal():
    run("final-security-normal", ["make", "check-security"], timeout=480)
    run("final-efficiency-normal", ["make", "check-efficiency"], timeout=180)
    run("final-session-controls-normal", ["make", "check-session-controls"], timeout=300)
    run("final-detach-normal", ["make", "check-security-detach"], timeout=180)
    extra = ["test_summary", "test_dcc", "test_editor", "test_nicks", "test_credentials", "test_app"]
    run("final-extra-units-build", ["make"]+["build/"+n for n in extra], timeout=180)
    for name in extra:
        run("final-"+name, ["./build/"+name])
    commands = [
        ("cli", ["tests/test_idle_cli.py"]),
        ("commands-manual", ["tests/test_idle_commands.py"]),
        ("terminal-offline", ["tests/test_idle_terminal.py", "--offline-only"]),
        ("context", ["tests/test_idle_context.py"]),
        ("setup", ["tests/test_idle_setup.py"]),
        ("setup-async", ["tests/test_setup_async.py", "--mode", "one"]),
        ("setup-paths", ["tests/test_setup_paths.py", "--mode", "one"]),
        ("autojoin-reconnect", ["tests/test_autojoin.py", "--mode", "onekey", "--binary", "./onekeyirc"]),
        ("idle-dcc", ["tests/test_idle_dcc.py"]),
        ("rename", ["tests/test_rename.py", "--onekey", "./onekeyirc"]),
        ("wrapping", ["tests/test_idle_wrapping.py", "--binary", "./onekeyirc"]),
    ]
    for name, args in commands:
        run("final-"+name, ["python3"]+args, timeout=300)
    names = ("direct_connect_save_and_reuse", "supplied_server_does_not_prompt_for_nick",
             "paste_and_review", "review_screen_bounds", "line_mode_live_tail_and_toggle",
             "direct_limit_and_bounds", "help_reader_preserves_chat_and_command_context",
             "output_format_and_persistence", "presence_departure_messages",
             "command_destination_is_pinned", "clear_keeps_other_view_history",
             "slow_terminal_keeps_network_alive", "catchup_memory_fallback",
             "catchup_from_last_sent", "main_chat_scrollback_keys")
    code = "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'tests'); import test_idle_terminal as t\n"
    code += "for n in "+repr(names)+":\n print('RUN '+n,flush=True); getattr(t,n)(); print('PASS '+n,flush=True)\n"
    run("final-terminal-live-supported", ["python3", "-c", code], timeout=600)
    run("final-native-session-probe", ["python3", "tests/test_session_hangup.py",
        "--binary", "./onekeyirc"], accepted=(77,), timeout=30)


def refresh_manual():
    # Only the full manual's release metadata changed after the first build.
    for label in ("normal", "sanitize"):
        previous = next(r for r in reversed(records)
                        if r["name"] == "final-vip-idle-harness-"+label+"-build")
        run("final-vip-idle-manual-"+label+"-build", previous["command"], cwd=VIP)
        full = subprocess.check_output([str(OUT/("vipirc-idle-"+label)), "--manual"], env=ENV)
        assert full == (VIP/"doc/manual.txt").read_bytes()
    minimal = subprocess.check_output([str(OUT/"vipirc-idle-normal"), "-i", "--manual"], env=ENV)
    (VIP/"doc/vipirc-idle-manual.txt").write_bytes(minimal)
    hashes = json.loads((OUT/"final-binary-hashes.json").read_text())
    for label in ("normal", "sanitize"):
        p = OUT/("vipirc-idle-"+label)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Record compiler analyzer coverage and diagnostics without hiding failures."""
import hashlib
import json
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
import sys
import time

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
TREE = ROOT / "irc-security-followup-work/onekeyirc-0.1.26"
OUT = ROOT / "irc-security-followup-validation/static"
OUT.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
RESULT = OUT / "results.json"
records = json.loads(RESULT.read_text()) if RESULT.exists() else []
base = ["cc", "-D_POSIX_C_SOURCE=200809L", "-D_XOPEN_SOURCE=700",
        "-D_XOPEN_SOURCE_EXTENDED=1", "-DONEKEY_ONLY", "-std=c11",
        "-Wall", "-Wextra", "-Wpedantic", "-Wformat=2", "-fanalyzer",
        "-fdiagnostics-format=json", "-Isrc", "-O0", "-c"]
for name in (sys.argv[1:] or ["editor", "protocol", "commands", "nicks", "client", "summary", "idle", "app", "idle_commands"]):
    source = TREE / "src" / (name + ".c")
    started = time.monotonic()
    command = base + [str(source), "-o", str(OUT / (name + ".o"))]
    print("ANALYZE " + name, flush=True)
    try:
        run = subprocess.run(command, cwd=TREE, capture_output=True, timeout=180)
        output = run.stdout + run.stderr
        code = run.returncode
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as error:
        output = (error.stdout or b"") + (error.stderr or b"")
        code = "TIMEOUT"
    log = OUT / (name + ".log")
    if log.exists():
        previous = OUT / (name + "-previous.log")
        previous.write_bytes(log.read_bytes())
        for record in records:
            if record["log"] == log.name: record["log"] = previous.name
    log.write_bytes(output)
    records.append({"source": str(source.relative_to(ROOT)),
                    "sha256": hashlib.sha256(source.read_bytes()).hexdigest(),
                    "command": command, "exit_code": code,
                    "seconds": round(time.monotonic()-started,3), "log": str(log.relative_to(OUT))})
    RESULT.write_text(json.dumps(records, indent=2)+"\n")
    print("DONE " + name + " " + str(code), flush=True)
